Subject: Cobalt Health — model fit, quant tradeoffs & throughput SLA (post-call next steps)

Alice / Ryan — thanks again for the call earlier. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, our recommended model/quantization approaches for the pilot, risks we want to validate, and proposed next steps + owners. I kept things operational so your engineering and procurement teams can act on them quickly.

Call highlights (what you told us)
- Primary workload: clinical summarization + patient Q&A for triage; median input ~1.2k tokens, 95th ~3.8k tokens.
- SLA target: 99th percentile latency <= 750ms for 1–2 concurrent user flows; peak throughput bursts up to ~60 qps for background batch summarization jobs.
- Quality tolerance: very low false-positive hallucinations on clinical facts; you prefer conservative responses.

Redwood initial model/quant recommendations (pilot scope)
1) Baseline (quality-focused): Llama-2-70b-chat (FP16) — best raw accuracy on our healthcare prompt set; recommended for critical triage queries where accuracy is paramount.
2) Throughput / cost baseline: Mistral-30B / MPT-30B (AWQ 4-bit) — materially lower per-token cost and good latency when using prefix/KV caching for recurring prompts.
3) Middle ground (recommended pilot split): Llama-2-33b (GPTQ 4-bit) with stricter decoding constraints for the triage channel; reserve Llama-2-70b for anomaly/complex cases.
4) FP8 (experimental): FP8 on Ampere/Instinct can unlock ~1.6x throughput vs FP16 but we observed a small drop on specific named-entity fidelity tests — treat as a stretch goal and only after pilot microbench.

Key tradeoffs & concerns
- AWQ (aggressive quant) gives the best cost/throughput but some prompt patterns (long clinical histories) showed a degradation in entity recall in our internal tests.
- GPTQ is a good compromise but requires careful per-layer tuning; out-of-the-box GPTQ variants can still have subtle regression on rare entity formats (labs, med codes).
- FP8 seems promising on the hardware you described (A100 Gen2 in your cloud region) but we want to validate numerical stability for temperature-sensitive outputs.

Actionable next steps (owners & dates)
1) Customer microbench with your prompt set (deliverable: runbook + raw results CSV) — Owner: Ryan (Cobalt) + Redwood infra (Marissa) — target start: 2027-11-10, complete by 2027-11-12.
2) Redwood to run three config microbenches (L70-FP16, L33-GPTQ-4, M30-AWQ-4) using your promptset and the same seed; include throughput @ batch sizes 1/4/8 and 95th/99th latency histograms. Owner: Marissa Cole — target: 2027-11-12. Attachment: cobalt_benchmarks_v1.csv (stub).
3) Quality regression harness: we propose a 250-case golden set (clinical QA / hallucination checks) and automated metric: factuality precision, answer completeness score, instruction adherence. Owner: Monica Patel (Redwood) + Alice — target to share seed promptset by 2027-11-09 end-of-day. Attachment: cobalt_promptset_v3.txt (stub).
4) Pilot config doc + canary rollout plan (including fallback to L70-FP16 with autoscaling rules) — Owner: Jonas Weber — draft by 2027-11-15. Attachment: poc_scope_and_timeline.pdf (stub).

Requested quick decisions from Cobalt (help us prioritize pilot knobs)
- Priority channel: should we prioritize latency for triage UI (tight SLO) or long-running batch summarization (throughput)?
- Will you accept a hybrid routing policy (fast path on AWQ/GPTQ + fallback to FP16 L70 for safety-critical prompts)?

I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the microbench kickoff and upload the demo recording + initial benchmark artifacts to the Drive link below. Thanks — Jonas

Subject: Re: Cobalt Health — model fit, quant tradeoffs & throughput SLA (post-call next steps)

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful and super actionable. Quick answers:
- Priority channel: triage UI latency is the immediate blocker for pilot—we need P99 < 750ms for interactive triage experience. Batch summarization can tolerate higher latency and will be scheduled outside peak hours.
- Hybrid routing: yes we like the hybrid approach. Route common/simple templates to the AWQ/GPTQ fast path and escalate to L70-FP16 for anything flagged "clinical-uncertain" by the classifier.

Ryan and I will start the microbench run on 11/10. I will upload our golden 250-case set (PHI redacted) to the Drive share by tonight. Also FYI procurement wants an initial SOW stub for hosting and data handling rules.

—Alice
